unit.why: A single anecdote, told by the son of R. Mordechai of Neschiz, about his father giving away the money he had saved for an etrog to a water-carrier whose horse had died.

stories.start_quote: סיפר מר מנשחיז שאביו הגאון מוהר״מ זצל"ה
stories.summary_en: R. Mordechai of Neschiz saved for a long time to buy an etrog, but on his way to Brody he gave all six roubles to a weeping water-carrier whose horse had died, saying that this too is God's commandment; in the end a beautiful etrog was brought to his home.

quotes: ועמד הרב ונתן לו הששה רו״כ
tags.why: He gives his etrog money to the poor water-carrier.
The tale illustrates the tzaddik's charity and self-sacrifice.

quotes: וכי מה הוא החילוק אתרוג הוא מצות ה׳ וזהו ג״כ מצות ה׳ היא
tags.why: He states that helping the needy is as much a mitzvah as the etrog.
The water-carrier weeps over his dead horse.

quotes: עד שקיבץ לו על אתרוג של מצוה
tags.why: The etrog for Sukkot frames the story.

quotes: ונסע לקנות אתרוג לבראד ופגע בשואב מים אחד
tags.why: The encounter takes place on his journey to Brody.

quotes: והביאו לו לביתו אתרוג יפה ומהודר עד מאד
tags.why: The unexpected arrival of a fine etrog is implied as a reward; it is not explicitly called a miracle.
The tale is framed as told by the tzaddik's son.

quotes: אתרוג הוא מצות ה׳ וזהו ג״כ מצות ה׳ היא
tags.why: He weighs one mitzvah against another; the point is closer to ethics than law.

missing_concepts: Commandment of the four species / etrog (hiddur mitzvah)
